scope: Selected primary passages and object records were consulted through web retrieval. A narrative's speaker is not automatically an independently documented historical person. Ancient translations, modern scholarly arguments, museum inscriptions and authorial proposals remain distinct. No unpublished manuscript collation or new investigation of living individuals is claimed.

sources.title: Josephus, Against Apion 1, translated by William Whiston
sources.kind: Ancient testimony and attributed earlier source
sources.locator: Book 1, discussion of Manetho and the shepherd rulers, especially 73-105 in continuous numbering
sources.scope: Selected discussion of the departure and Josephus's identification was consulted. Manetho is mediated by Josephus; this is not a contemporary document establishing Moses's date.

sources.title: Joseph Blenkinsopp, The Midianite-Kenite Hypothesis Revisited and the Origins of Judah (2008)
sources.locator: Journal for the Study of the Old Testament 33(2), 131-153; DOI 10.1177/0309089208099253
sources.scope: Abstract only. It identifies four evidential bases of the hypothesis. The restricted full article was not read, and the abstract does not establish Moses's beliefs about death.

sources.title: Rami Arav, The Golden Calf: Bull-El Worship
sources.locator: Published February 16, 2022; argument about northern Bull-El/Yahweh representation
sources.scope: The argument and its use of Exodus 32 were consulted. This is a specific iconographic and literary interpretation, not the only established meaning of every calf image.

sources.title: The Met, Apis Bull Statuette, object 17.190.62
sources.locator: Late Period statuette, dated 664-343 BCE; description of the earlier Apis cult
sources.scope: Object description and account of the living bull, Ptah temple, regeneration and burial were consulted. The object's date is not a date for Exodus, and no direct dependence on this particular artifact is alleged.

sources.title: Exodus 2, World English Bible
sources.scope: Midianite setting, priestly household and Zipporah's marriage in the narrative. This does not independently verify a population migration or every historical detail.

sources.title: Exodus 3, World English Bible
sources.scope: The burning-bush narrative and divine-name disclosure. Jethro is not the named speaker of the disclosure in this passage.

sources.title: Exodus 6, World English Bible
sources.scope: El Shaddai, Yahweh and the narrative promise. The comparison distinguishes textual wording from harmonization and historical source reconstruction.

sources.title: Exodus 18, World English Bible
sources.scope: Jethro's blessing, sacrifice and meal. Prior transmission, recognition and conversion are not all explicitly narrated by those actions.

sources.title: Exodus 32, World English Bible
sources.scope: Aaron's making of the calf, the announced festival, Moses's destruction of the image and the Levites' subsequent violence. These are distinct actors and actions within the account.

sources.title: Genesis 37, World English Bible
sources.scope: Jacob's reference to Sheol. It refutes absolute silence about the dead but does not define every feature of a later judgment system.

sources.title: Genesis 50, World English Bible
sources.scope: Embalming, burial and remembered obligations. Absence of condemnation in this narrative is not an endorsement of every Egyptian religious practice.

sources.title: Leviticus 21, World English Bible
sources.scope: Different rules for ordinary priests and the high priest concerning deceased relatives. Ritual status is distinguished from a conclusion that all contact with death is morally evil.

sources.title: Deuteronomy 5, World English Bible
sources.scope: Rest for dependents and the appeal to Egyptian servitude. The study does not claim an independent demonstration of universal implementation.

sources.title: Deuteronomy 15, World English Bible
sources.scope: Seventh-year debt release, the foreigner distinction, aid and release of Hebrew servants. These are not silently collapsed into Levitical Jubilee rules.

sources.title: Deuteronomy 24, World English Bible
sources.scope: Collateral, wages, justice and gleaning, including references to foreigners and Egyptian servitude. The moral interpretation retains the actual legal categories.

sources.title: Leviticus 25, World English Bible
sources.scope: Jubilee, divine land ownership, redemption, housing exceptions and permanent foreign slavery. The chapter is not presented as a universal abolition law.

sources.title: Luke 16, World English Bible
sources.scope: Mammon and the rich man/Lazarus narrative, especially its appeal to Moses and the prophets. The study identifies its interpretation rather than treating the parable as an observed journey through the afterlife.

sources.title: Mark 12, World English Bible
sources.scope: Resurrection debate and invocation of the burning bush, followed by agreement with a scribe concerning the commands. The narrative does not imply one uniform hostile Jewish position.

sources.title: Mark 10, World English Bible
sources.scope: Interpretation of Mosaic divorce permission through creation, and the wealth/discipleship encounter. These do not demonstrate complete identity of every Mosaic and Jesus tradition.

sources.title: Mark 11, World English Bible
sources.scope: Temple action and its Isaiah/Jeremiah citations. The account is not a detailed audit of exchange rates or every individual's institutional motive.

sources.title: Jeremiah 7, World English Bible
sources.scope: Wrongdoing, sanctuary confidence and the den-of-robbers image. The text supports a critique from within the tradition, not a blanket judgment on a people.

sources.title: Josephus, Antiquities 18.1.3-4, William Whiston translation
sources.locator: Continuous numbering 18.12-17; introductory Pharisee and Sadducee comparison
sources.scope: The doctrines and status claims were read. Josephus's generalized account is not a psychological interview with every member or a neutral survey of all Judaism.

sources.title: War Scroll excerpt, Center for Online Judaic Studies
sources.locator: Passage describing the Kittim and combat of human and heavenly forces
sources.scope: The excerpt establishes that the adversaries are not simply defined by wealth. The site's approximate title date is not adopted as a settled date for all textual layers.

sources.title: National Gallery of Victoria, Mortuary stela from the tomb of 'Iti
sources.locator: Accession D84-1982; late First Intermediate Period/early Dynasty XI, 2125-2055 BCE
sources.scope: The inscription connects assistance to familiar and unfamiliar people with enduring on earth and in the necropolis. It is a public self-presentation, not independent verification that every deed occurred.

sources.title: The Met, False Door of the Royal Sealer Neferiu
sources.kind: Museum object and translated inscription in audio transcript
sources.scope: Good-deed claims and funerary setting were consulted. The broad causal explanation of Old Kingdom collapse in the audio is not reproduced as a new historical finding.

sources.title: Ancient Egypt Research Associates, excavation overview
sources.locator: Lost City of the Pyramids and descriptions of crews, administrators and compulsory service
sources.scope: The research program and labor-organization descriptions were consulted. These distinguish categories of labor without proving all workers free or eliminating coercion from Egyptian history.

sources.title: Gustaf Dalman, Mammon, New Schaff-Herzog Encyclopedia, CCEL
sources.locator: Mammon entry following Mamre/Mamertus page heading
sources.scope: Wealth/possessions as lexical starting point and lack of a documented ancient deity by that name. Older disputed etymological proposals are not treated as established origins.

sources.title: Luke 12, World English Bible
sources.scope: Stored goods, mortality and giving. The ethical application to present institutions is this study's proposal, not a claim that the text names modern technologies.

sources.title: 1 Timothy 6, World English Bible
sources.scope: Instructions to the wealthy to share and avoid placing hope in uncertain riches. The text is a separate Christian witness, not a saying attributed directly to Jesus.

access_limitations: Direct retrieval of eBible Numbers 16 and 19 and one combined BibleGateway query failed; those pages are not used as freshly read evidence. Genesis 37 and Leviticus 21 supply the narrower comparisons actually made.
The supplied books by Smith, Miller, Hoffmeier, Wright and Meier have not been read in full in this pass. They are not cited as authenticating every claim in the pasted discussion.
The Egyptian Seed and Hyksos/Exodus proposals remain attributed research hypotheses. No new archaeology establishes a complete genealogy or a private belief of Moses.
